### 11.40 Compromised-password screening

`CompromisedPasswordValidator` is registered in the ASP.NET Core Identity validator pipeline, so administrator-created accounts, self-service password change, forced password remediation, seed-controlled password replacement, and one-time password reset cannot bypass the same rule. A deterministic local denylist always rejects common/default OPMS and administrative passwords, including when external screening is intentionally disabled for offline development. The login and settings surfaces state that common or breached values are rejected rather than presenting complexity alone as sufficient security.

Production enables a fail-closed `PwnedPasswordLookup`. It computes SHA-1 locally, sends only the first five hexadecimal characters to the configured HTTPS range endpoint, requests response padding, supplies the provider-required user agent, bounds the response size and timeout, ignores zero-count padding entries, and compares the remaining suffix locally. Neither the password nor its complete hash leaves the application. Successful prefix ranges are cached briefly without password/user association. The implementation follows the provider's documented [Pwned Passwords k-anonymity range protocol](https://haveibeenpwned.com/API/v3). Any provider failure blocks password creation/change/reset with a safe retry message in production. `CompromisedPasswordHealthCheck` also makes readiness unhealthy when fail-closed screening cannot reach the range service and reports degraded configuration if screening is enabled without fail-closed behavior.

Automated tests prove that only the five-character prefix is transmitted, the full hash and password are absent from the request, padding and user-agent headers are present, padded rows are ignored, occurrence thresholds are enforced, prefix results are cached, local common values are rejected without a network call, remote breach matches are rejected, fail-closed outages reject password writes, disabled development screening retains local protection, and production readiness fails on provider outage. Backend **123/123** tests pass with one SQL Server integration test explicitly skipped; frontend **101/101** tests pass across **26** files. TypeScript type-check, ESLint, backend/frontend production builds, and `git diff --check` pass. No schema migration or database-provider-specific application code was introduced; the SQL Server migration script remains **271,968 bytes**.

Compromised-password screening is repository-complete for local Identity. Authentication remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** pending configurable Entra ID/Active Directory/hybrid providers, administrator-facing authentication-policy governance, production distributed-session rehearsal, and browser penetration/CSRF acceptance.

### 11.41 Governed IDP plan and version lineage

IDP plans now carry both a record-level `PublicId` and a stable `PlanFamilyId`. A successor can reference one same-tenant predecessor and inherits its family identifier; independent plans start a new family. Plans also carry effective-from/effective-to dates, publication timestamp/reference, and RowVersion. The controller rejects reversed financial or effective periods, missing/cross-tenant predecessors, and successors that predate their predecessor. Transitioning a plan to Published requires an explicit publication reference and records the publication timestamp.

Every IDP plan version now has its own public ID, optional predecessor-version link, effective period, publication evidence, and RowVersion. Creating a version links it to the active predecessor, requires a later effective date within the parent plan's effective period, closes the predecessor's effective period, and leaves only the successor active. Hierarchy and plan-list responses expose the lineage without leaking internal foreign keys. The dashboard no longer performs synthetic plan or annual-review writes; it routes authorized users to a governed workspace. That workspace captures real plan identity, predecessor, effective dates, publication reference, version type/label/review year/change summary, and version effective/publication metadata.

Migration `20261002102623_V39IdpPlanLineage` first adds nullable legacy-bridge columns, deterministically backfills every existing plan family and version public ID, derives predecessor-version links by version order, closes inactive effective periods, and only then makes required columns non-null and creates indexes, checks, and restricted self-references. SQL Server keeps native generated `rowversion`; the shared EF model advances concurrency values for SQLite verification. No controller/domain code changes are required when the deployment connection remains SQL Server.

Frontend tests pass **2/2** for governed navigation and exact lineage payload transport. ### 11.43 Governed IDP KPI import and reconciliation

The optional import path now stages KPI definitions beneath an existing tenant-owned IDP plan through versioned `/api/v1/idp` endpoints. A client request ID and canonical server-side SHA-256 make staging idempotent. Each immutable staged row records the source payload, normalized candidate, current value, classification, validation detail, and expected KPI RowVersion. Reconciliation classifies every row as NEW, UNCHANGED, CHANGED, or INVALID and prevents commit until the entire batch is valid. Source-row uniqueness, count consistency, public identifiers, tenant ownership, and append-only evidence are also database-enforced.

Commit requires the original batch RowVersion and a reason, re-runs reconciliation against current records, rejects stale classifications or target versions, and applies every NEW/CHANGED row in one transaction. Stage and commit write audit evidence. Both browser capability checks and direct endpoints require the stable `IDP_INDICATOR.IMPORT` action, while tenant query filters prevent cross-municipality batch or row access. Manual and imported KPI creation use `IdpKpiDefinitionPolicy`, preventing validation drift; the workspace provides a downloadable CSV template, robust quoted-field parsing, reconciliation counts/details, commit controls, and recent batch history.

CSV and workspace/transport tests cover quoted input, typed validation, capability gating, idempotency, RowVersion, preview, and commit. ### 11.44 Governed withdrawal and no-hard-delete lifecycle

OPMS and IPMS targets and submissions now use an explicit withdrawal action rather than deletion. Each versioned endpoint requires a bounded governance reason and current RowVersion, evaluates the stable `OPMS_KPI.WITHDRAW`, `IPMS_KPI.WITHDRAW`, `OPMS_SUBMISSION.WITHDRAW`, or `IPMS_SUBMISSION.WITHDRAW` action against the record scope, and operates only inside the selected municipality. The target or submission is retained with actor/time/reason metadata while a separate `GovernedRecordLifecycleEvent` records the tenant, aggregate, action, actor, timestamp, reason and correlation identifier. The ledger has restricted foreign keys, a tenant query filter, and DbContext-level update/delete rejection.

Withdrawn targets cannot be edited or used for new submissions. Withdrawn submissions cannot be edited, scored, advanced through workflow, extended, uploaded to, or have evidence replaced; preservation operations such as authorized download, malware rescan, assessment, legal hold and governed retention disposal remain available where their independent policies permit them. Target and submission DELETE routes return 410 with the governed replacement contract. POE DELETE routes continue to reject destructive removal, their browser transport and controls were removed, and security permission registry entries can only be deactivated rather than physically deleted. The SPA replaces trash/delete actions with capability-gated withdrawal dialogs that require a reason and transport the current concurrency token while leaving the retained record visible.

### 11.46 Independent Technical Indicator Description module

Each municipality now controls two explicit settings: `TidEnabled` and `TidAllKpisRequired`. Disabling the optional module leaves every OPMS target and submission path unchanged. ### 11.50 Operational telemetry, readiness and response hardening

**Requirement:** R-52 / Phase 11 monitoring, health and security-test hardening.

**Implementation:** Every HTTP request now contributes to bounded `System.Diagnostics.Metrics` counters, an active-request gauge and duration histogram under meter `FTCERP.Host`, plus an `ActivitySource` named `FTCERP.Host.Operations`. Labels are deliberately limited to request method and response status class to avoid tenant, user, URL or record cardinality and disclosure. The existing validated correlation identifier is included in the structured logging scope and trace tag, while completion logs capture status and duration without request payloads or credentials. An in-process snapshot drives configurable failure-rate and average-duration readiness degradation after a minimum sample size. This supplies deterministic alert conditions without claiming that an external pager exists.

The readiness endpoint now returns stable machine-readable JSON containing only check name, status and duration; health descriptions, exceptions and data dictionaries are not exposed anonymously. Existing database, outbox, storage, malware-scanner, notification-channel and compromised-password checks remain part of readiness, while liveness intentionally avoids dependency probes. Default browser responses now include content-type, framing, referrer, feature-permission and restrictive content-security policies. Production thresholds are configuration, and the metrics/activity sources can be collected by standard .NET/OpenTelemetry deployment instrumentation without changing domain, controller, service, UI or database-provider code.

**Files/classes:** `Infrastructure/Observability/OperationalTelemetry.cs`, `Infrastructure/Health/OperationalTelemetryHealthCheck.cs`, `Infrastructure/Health/HealthResponseWriter.cs`, `Infrastructure/Security/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs`, `Program.cs`, `appsettings.json`, `appsettings.Production.json`, and `.env.example`.

**Migration:** None. The feature is provider-neutral and SQL Server deployment remains a configuration/migration operation; SQLite can continue to exercise repository behavior temporarily.

**API:** `GET /health/live` remains a dependency-free process probe. `GET /health/ready` executes all dependency and telemetry checks and emits a non-sensitive JSON contract suitable for an orchestrator or external monitor.

### 11.51 SQL Server backup and isolated recovery drill

**Requirement:** R-53 / Phase 11 recovery hardening.

**Implementation:** `tools/Invoke-OpmsSqlServerRecoveryDrill.ps1` provides an executable full recovery rehearsal for the deployment database engine. The script accepts its connection string only through a named environment variable, never prints the credential, requires an explicit destructive-drill acknowledgement, and refuses every server except the local SQL Express aliases and every source database except `OPMS_Development` or `OPMS_IntegrationTests`. It performs a copy-only compressed backup with checksum, `RESTORE VERIFYONLY`, parses the backup file list, restores to a randomized isolated database/files, executes `DBCC CHECKDB`, evaluates configurable RPO/RTO thresholds, and cleans up only that exact isolated database unless retention was explicitly requested. A versioned JSON evidence record captures timing and outcomes under the ignored `artifacts/recovery-drills` directory.

The operational runbook is: stop or quiesce write-producing test activity; set `OPMS_RECOVERY_CONNECTION_STRING` in the invoking process from a local secret; ensure `sqlcmd` is installed and the SQL Server service account can write the selected backup directory; run `pwsh ./tools/Invoke-OpmsSqlServerRecoveryDrill.ps1 -ConfirmLocalDestructiveRecoveryDrill`; inspect the exit code and JSON evidence; investigate any backup, checksum, restore, integrity, cleanup, RPO or RTO failure before release. Production/UAT operators must substitute an infrastructure-approved encrypted/off-site backup schedule and isolated recovery environment—the repository script deliberately refuses remote or production databases.

**Files/classes:** `tools/Invoke-OpmsSqlServerRecoveryDrill.ps1`, `.github/workflows/quality.yml`, `.gitignore`, and `.env.example`.

**Migration:** None. The drill targets SQL Server backup semantics directly. Temporary SQLite development remains supported by application configuration, while moving to SQL Server requires configuration and existing EF migrations rather than domain, controller, service or UI changes.

**API:** None; recovery credentials and commands are intentionally excluded from HTTP surfaces.

**Tests:** `-ValidateOnly` emits the script's explicit server/database allowlist, safety gate and operation contract without reading credentials or mutating a database; CI executes this validation on every change. PowerShell parser validation and the non-mutating contract check pass locally. The live backup/restore branch was not executed because an approved reachable SQL Server test instance is not available in this run.

**Status:** R-53 advances from **NOT VERIFIABLE** to **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT**. The repository now contains a guarded and auditable recovery drill, but compliance requires retained evidence from successful scheduled backups, checksum verification, isolated restores, integrity checks and measured RPO/RTO in approved SQL Server infrastructure, plus a witnessed disaster-recovery/failover exercise.

### 11.52 Route-level loading and executable frontend performance budget

**Requirement:** Phase 11 performance hardening and R-54 automated quality enforcement.

The budget is deliberately below the prior monolith while leaving controlled headroom for the largest charting route.

**API:** None.

The production build emits multiple route chunks, and `npm run check:bundle` verifies the **450 KiB** maximum against the actual build artifacts. The complete frontend and backend test suites remain required CI gates.

Phase 11 performance remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** pending representative browser performance baselines, server/API load and saturation tests, slow-query/index analysis against native SQL Server, and bounded server pagination for remaining large collection endpoints.

### 11.53 Cookie-request integrity, API throttling and controlled seed secrets

**Requirement:** R-10 through R-13 and Phase 11 security hardening/testing.

**Implementation:** State-changing `/api` requests now require the `X-OPMS-Request: same-origin` browser header unless they use an explicit Bearer token. Combined with Secure production, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict authentication cookies and the existing allowlisted credentialed CORS policy, this blocks cross-site form/image mutation attempts while retaining non-browser API-client compatibility. The SPA sends the header on initial, upload, refresh and retried requests. Every controller endpoint also uses a fixed-window user/IP API policy in addition to the stricter authentication policy; rejected requests return 429 before controller work.

The security audit also removed the tracked `Credentials.md` plaintext credential dump and prevents it from being re-added. Controlled seeding no longer contains a password or administrator-email fallback. Administrator and optional demo-user passwords must be supplied through local/deployment secrets and meet the 12-character baseline. Demo identities require a separate `SeedData:DemoUsersEnabled` opt-in. Newly seeded identities must change their initial password, while an existing administrator or demo identity is left untouched—no password reset, profile rewrite, role rewrite or scope rewrite occurs on a later run. Seed creation failure is explicit rather than silently continuing with a partially governed identity.

**Files/classes:** `Infrastructure/Security/CsrfProtectionMiddleware.cs`, `Program.cs`, `ClientApp/src/api/api.ts`, `Infrastructure/Persistence/Seed/DbInitializer.cs`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, and `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs`. The insecure tracked `Credentials.md` artifact is removed.

**Migration:** None. These controls are provider-neutral; deployment to SQL Server remains configuration-only for application code.

**API:** All unsafe `/api` methods enforce the same-origin header for cookie sessions; Bearer-token integrations remain supported. All mapped controllers inherit the `api` rate-limit policy, while authentication endpoints retain their stricter named policy.

**Tests:** Seven backend CSRF tests cover safe methods, missing-header rejection, accepted same-origin mutation, Bearer compatibility and non-API pass-through. Four controlled-secret tests reject missing/blank/short values and accept an explicit strong local secret. The cookie-session browser tests verify the header on login, refresh and retry while confirming that no Bearer token or token body is exposed. The complete backend suite passes **172/172** with one native SQL Server acceptance test explicitly skipped; the complete frontend suite passes **129/129** across **34** files. R-13 advances to **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** because the current tree no longer contains the credential dump or seed defaults, but repository history and any environment that used the exposed values require owner-led credential rotation, optional history remediation, and production managed-secret injection evidence. ### 11.55 General business-mutation idempotency

**Requirement:** R-46 / retry-safe POST mutations.

**Implementation:** Every authenticated non-authentication API `POST`, including JSON and multipart business mutations, now requires an `Idempotency-Key` containing 8-128 safe characters. The middleware runs after authentication, tenant resolution and authorization. It hashes the complete query/body stream, then atomically acquires a durable identity derived from municipality/system scope, user, method, normalized route and caller key. An identical completed request replays status, content type, location, ETag and body with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; reuse with a changed body/query returns 409; an in-flight duplicate returns 409 plus `Retry-After`; and an exception after possible side effects is marked ambiguous and cannot be re-executed with the same key. Authentication endpoints are intentionally excluded because session-cookie responses must never be persisted or replayed.

`IdempotencyRequest` stores only request hashes—not request bodies—and retains replay bodies for a configurable 24-hour window. Records are tenant-filtered, FK-bound to user/municipality, concurrency protected, state constrained and uniquely indexed by a fixed SHA-256 identity hash, avoiding SQL Server composite-index width limits. A hosted cleanup worker removes expired records. The SPA generates one key per POST user action and reuses that exact key if cookie-session refresh causes an automatic retry. Swagger declares the required header on protected business POST operations.

SQLite uses the shared portable concurrency mechanism; deployment to SQL Server remains configuration plus migrations only.

The browser session test proves one generated key survives a 401/refresh/retry sequence. The complete idempotent SQL Server migration script generates at **376,498 bytes** and contains the ledger table, unique identity-hash index and generated `rowversion`.

**Status:** R-46 is **COMPLIANT** at repository level. Native SQL Server concurrent duplicate-request execution remains deployment acceptance evidence; no domain, controller, service or UI code changes are required when changing the configured database provider.

### 11.56 Municipality-configurable enterprise authentication

**Requirement:** R-09 / LOCAL, MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID, ACTIVE_DIRECTORY and HYBRID authentication without a hard-coded provider.

**Implementation:** Each municipality now persists a concurrency-governed, effective-dated `AuthenticationConfiguration` family whose versions each own an immutable `AuthenticationPolicy` snapshot. The mode controls whether local password sign-in is permitted and which deployment-registered enterprise provider may be challenged. Provider registrations are loaded from deployment configuration/secrets, require a unique safe code and callback path, accept only HTTPS authorities, and support Microsoft Entra ID or standards-based Active Directory federation through authorization-code OIDC with PKCE, issuer validation and short-lived correlation/nonce state. Client secrets are never stored in the application database or returned through an API. Switching between SQLite development and SQL Server deployment remains configuration-only; the domain, controller, service and UI code is shared.

External account linking is deliberately closed: an administrator must pre-provision a `UserAuthenticator` for an existing active user in the same municipality. A validated callback first resolves an existing fixed provider/issuer/subject digest; an unbound pre-provision may bind exactly once only when its expected email matches the validated claim. Email alone never creates a user or links an arbitrary account. Unique hashes reject duplicate external identities, disabled and cross-municipality accounts are denied, and authentication changes use `RowVersion`. `AuthenticationEvent` is tenant-filtered and append-only; configuration, provisioning and status changes also append the normal audit trail with the governance reason. External success issues the same hashed-refresh, database-governed internal session used by local authentication.

The public login screen discovers only the municipality display name, whether local sign-in is enabled, and non-secret provider code/name/kind. It redirects to a fixed provider challenge and safely resumes the cookie-only session after the fixed local callback. The lazy-loaded Authentication Governance page selects the mode/provider, creates chronological successor versions rather than overwriting policy values, exposes bounded searchable version history, pre-provisions users, enables/disables authenticators and displays recent authentication events. Dynamic permissions `AUTHENTICATION.READ`, `AUTHENTICATION.CONFIGURE`, `AUTHENTICATION.LINK_IDENTITIES` and `AUTHENTICATION.VIEW_EVENTS`, plus a permission-protected navigation item, keep UI and direct API enforcement aligned.

### 11.58 Dynamic municipality authentication-policy enforcement

**Requirement:** R-10 through R-12 / municipality-governed password, MFA, lockout and session controls that take effect without recompilation.

**Implementation:** The stored, concurrency-governed `AuthenticationPolicy` is now resolved for the authenticated user's municipality on every relevant operation. Local Identity password creation, reset and change use the municipality minimum length in addition to the global complexity and compromised-password validators. Failed local sign-in uses the configured attempt threshold and lockout duration; the global Identity threshold is retained only as a safe ceiling above the permitted municipality range. New tenant users inherit the configured first-login password-change requirement without rewriting existing administrator-managed accounts.

JWT/session issuance and validation apply the current municipality idle timeout, absolute lifetime and maximum concurrent-session count. A stricter policy therefore affects effective session validation without recompilation. Each refresh-token family records a bounded authentication method, exposes it in account session administration and preserves it through rotation. Local TOTP enrollment is required for all or only privileged local users according to policy; an externally authenticated Entra ID or AD-federated session is not incorrectly forced into the local TOTP flow. Access tokens retain the normalized authentication-method claim. Existing refresh sessions are conservatively backfilled as `LOCAL` during upgrade.

The Authentication Governance UI now versions every bounded policy value rather than silently preserving hidden defaults or overwriting the effective policy: minimum password length, failed-attempt threshold, lockout duration, privileged/all-local MFA, first-login password change, idle timeout, absolute timeout and concurrent-session maximum. RowVersion and governance-reason handling remain on the administration contract, and a bounded searchable ledger exposes every preserved configuration/policy version. The account settings session list identifies the authentication method used for each active session.

### 11.59 Standard RFC 7807 API errors and validation

**Requirement:** R-44 and the API contract baseline / consistent 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 415, 422, 429 and 500 behavior.

**Implementation:** Successful API calls retain the established typed `ApiResponse<T>` contract. A global always-run MVC result filter now converts every failed legacy `ApiResponse<T>` returned by any controller into RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` without requiring hundreds of error paths to be rewritten independently. Automatic `[ApiController]` binding, non-nullability and DataAnnotations failures use field-keyed `ValidationProblemDetails`. Empty framework authentication, authorization, routing, media-type, payload-size and rate-limit responses are filled by the centralized status-code pipeline. CSRF, tenant resolution, password-change, MFA-enrollment and idempotency middleware use the same writer.

Every problem carries status, title, request instance, a stable machine code and the validated request correlation ID. Required mappings include `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, `ACCESS_DENIED`, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `STATE_CONFLICT`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `INTERNAL_ERROR`; controlled middleware may supply a more specific code without central customization overwriting it. The exception handler maps explicit authorization, concurrency and application-validation exceptions, while unexpected exceptions—including framework `ArgumentException` failures—return a sanitized 500 and never expose infrastructure detail. The exception/status pipeline now wraps all downstream security, telemetry, CSRF, authentication, tenant, authorization and controller processing.

Swagger adds `application/problem+json` documentation for the standard failure statuses on every operation. The SPA transport already supported ProblemDetails and now also preserves stable code and body/header correlation evidence while flattening field errors into the existing UI error list. Existing screens therefore remain compatible as the server failure shape becomes uniform.

**Files/classes:** `Infrastructure/Security/ApiProblemDetails.cs`, `Infrastructure/OpenApi/ProblemDetailsOperationFilter.cs`, `Infrastructure/Security/CorrelationIdMiddleware.cs`, `Infrastructure/Security/CsrfProtectionMiddleware.cs`, `Infrastructure/Security/TenantContext.cs`, `Infrastructure/Security/IdempotencyMiddleware.cs`, `Infrastructure/Auth/MfaRequirementPolicy.cs`, `Infrastructure/Auth/PasswordChangePolicy.cs`, `API/Responses/AuthResponses.cs`, `Program.cs`, `ClientApp/src/api/api.ts`, and `ClientApp/src/types/index.ts`.

**Migration:** None. The contract is provider-neutral and requires no database, domain, controller, service or UI variation between SQLite development and SQL Server deployment.

**Tests:** Filter tests prove legacy failure conversion and success-response preservation. Model-state tests prove field-keyed validation. Status-code theories cover all required mappings. Middleware tests prove RFC 7807 content, specific-code preservation and correlation evidence. Exception tests prove unexpected argument/configuration detail is sanitized as a 500. The client test proves detail, code, flattened validation messages and correlation evidence survive transport normalization. A disposable SQLite-hosted HTTP smoke run exercised the real routing/authentication/filter/formatter stack and returned: 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` with `Email`/`Password` field errors, 400 `CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED`, and 401 `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED`, all as `application/problem+json` with the caller's correlation ID. Disposable processes and database files were removed afterward. The full suites pass **209/209 backend** and **135/135 frontend** tests, with only the explicitly environment-gated native SQL Server acceptance test skipped. Release build, TypeScript, ESLint, production build, 66-chunk bundle budget and model/snapshot consistency pass.

**Status:** R-44 is **COMPLIANT** at repository level. Contract consumers should use the stable problem code rather than matching human-readable detail. Deployed gateway/proxy behavior and external integration conformance remain UAT acceptance evidence.

### 11.66 Central performance-consolidation compatibility engine

**Requirement:** V3.9 sections 5.6, 11.7-11.10 and 15.1; final assessment area 9.

**Implementation:** `PerformanceConsolidationEngine` is the single server-side authority for determining whether source-period values may safely produce a Mid-Term or Annual suggestion. It implements the nine specified calculation types. `SUM` and `AVERAGE` perform canonical numeric aggregation; `LATEST_VALUE` selects the latest canonical source; `CUMULATIVE` and `REVERSE_CUMULATIVE` default to the latest valid cumulative position. `NON_CUMULATIVE`, `REVERSE_NON_CUMULATIVE`, `ZERO_BASED` and `MANUAL` fail closed unless an explicit municipality rule selects a safe primitive operation. An explicit configured rule may also override a cumulative default without recompilation. `PerformanceTargetDerivationService` applies the V3.9 Mid-Term precedence rule: a valid approved source Mid-Term target wins without derivation metadata; when it is absent, Q1 and Q2 flow through the central engine and return the canonical target, `IsSystemDerivedTarget`, source-period list, effective derivation rule and immutable original system-suggested value needed by persistence.

The engine accepts an ordered required-period set and only consumes submitted, effective source values. Missing values default to blocking and are never silently converted to zero; explicit block, manual, ignore and treat-as-zero policies are represented separately. Source and destination units must match until an explicit conversion rule exists. Every value and generated result is passed through the canonical performance-unit engine. Mathematical aggregation rejects dates, ratios, qualitative and binary values, while latest-value selection can safely preserve their canonical representation. Every refusal returns a stable code and user-facing explanation suitable for the frontend rather than requiring duplicated React calculation logic.

Persistence now follows the V3.9 ownership model. Nine stable calculation-type masters are seeded and referenced by OPMS/IPMS KPIs. A tenant-filtered municipality policy stores an optional safe primitive override, explicit missing-value policy, derived-target override permission, annual-target derivation flag and provider-portable `RowVersion`. Normalized period targets store `IsSystemDerivedTarget`, source periods, the effective calculation type and the original system-suggested target. OPMS/IPMS submissions store `SystemSuggestedActualPerformance` separately from final `ActualPerformance`, the edited flag, calculation type, generation timestamp and editor/time/reason metadata. `PerformanceSuggestionEvent` is a tenant-owned append-only ledger for generated, accepted and edited values with source periods, actor and correlation evidence. Database checks require exactly one OPMS/IPMS submission per event and complete edit metadata whenever the edited flag is set.

Versioned routes under `/api/v1/performance-consolidation` expose the active calculation-type catalogue and the current tenant's complete policy projection. Policy creation/update requires the dynamic `OPMS_KPI.CONFIGURE_CONSOLIDATION` action, a municipality context and an explicit governance reason. The server permits only `SUM`, `AVERAGE` or `LATEST_VALUE` as configured primitive overrides, validates the missing-value enum, protects updates with `RowVersion`, returns conflicts for stale or duplicate writes and writes contextual create/edit audit evidence. Read routes independently require `OPMS_KPI.READ`; hiding a future administration view therefore cannot bypass direct API authorization.

The OPMS and IPMS submission routes now complete the runtime path. Mid-Term generation resolves exactly Q1 and Q2; Annual generation resolves exactly Q1-Q4. Only canonical `SUBMITTED`, timestamped, active source submissions participate. Missing or duplicate period configuration, missing source values, incompatible units, invalid destination targets, withdrawn/non-editable submissions and unsafe calculation rules fail closed with stable explanations. Generation is idempotent: the first suggestion is retained, concurrent generation is protected by submission `RowVersion`, and later attempts do not create duplicate ledger entries. Accepting the suggestion or saving an authorised deviation recalculates canonical actual, variance, achievement percentage and target-achieved state from the governed destination period target. A deviation requires a reason and never overwrites the original suggestion.

Versioned OPMS/IPMS endpoints generate suggestions, save final consolidated actuals and return ordered immutable history. Entity UPDATE/READ and `ActualPerformance` member permissions are independently checked against the submission scope, so a hidden control cannot authorize a direct request. Suggestion fields are redacted with the protected actual member. The submission workspace displays the original suggestion, final actual, generated/edited metadata, edit reason and event history for Mid-Term and Annual periods; authorised owners can generate, accept or edit, while client controls enforce the reason rule and the API remains authoritative.

**Tests:** Thirty-one engine/derivation tests cover the defined behavior of all nine types, configured municipality rules, default missing-value protection, explicit ignore/zero handling, submitted/effective eligibility, incompatible units, invalid sources, unsafe nonnumeric aggregation, canonical nonnumeric latest values, destination-unit result validation, duplicate-period rejection, explicit-target precedence, complete derived-target metadata and invalid-explicit-target refusal. Three relational persistence tests prove all nine seeded codes, tenant-policy isolation and uniqueness, portable RowVersion concurrency, separate suggestion/final fields and append-only history. Six policy-controller tests prove authorized create/update, RowVersion transport, contextual audit, the complete policy projection, rejection of unsafe overrides and direct-call denial without the dynamic permission. Four relational runtime tests prove Mid-Term sum, Annual average, exact source-period ordering, missing-quarter refusal without mutation, one-time generation, acceptance/edit history, preservation of the original suggestion, metric recalculation and direct API denial when member permission is absent. The complete backend suite passes **281/281** with one explicitly environment-gated native SQL Server acceptance test skipped. The frontend suite passes **140/140 across 42 files**; TypeScript and ESLint pass. The Release host build passes with zero warnings and zero errors. SQL Server model/snapshot consistency passes, and the **417,488-byte** idempotent migration script contains the new tables, fields, checks, indexes, seed data and restricted foreign keys.

**Status:** The central calculation, governed policy, persistence, runtime submission API, immutable ledger and SPA suggestion/final-value experience make final assessment area 9 **COMPLIANT** at repository level. Target derivation invocation during every import remains tracked under normalized target/import areas 6 and 18 rather than weakening the completed actual-consolidation requirement.

### 11.67 Configurable Internal Audit assessment models

**Requirement:** V3.9 sections 4.10A, 17.3 and 18.1, including the acceptance scenarios in the Internal Audit assessment-model matrix; final assessment areas 13 and 15.

**Implementation:** `InternalAuditAssessmentConfiguration` is an effective-dated, tenant-owned, municipality-financial-year-specific version record. Administrators select either Detailed IA Assessment or Satisfactory / Not Satisfactory through Workflow Governance. Replacing a selection requires the current RowVersion, closes the predecessor, appends a successor and writes contextual audit evidence; the database enforces one current selection and unique version numbers. Existing submissions resolve the applicable model through their pinned workflow definition and financial year, so a later selection never rewrites an earlier assessment.

`InternalAuditAssessment` is an append-only assessment/reassessment ledger linked to the exact configuration and workflow instance. A reassessment must reference the latest prior assessment, while a filtered unique successor constraint prevents competing branches. The simplified model accepts exactly IA Assessment Status and required IA Detailed Observation. `NOT_SATISFACTORY` requires a future response due date and atomically creates a scoped `PerformanceRfi`, Internal Audit notification/outbox evidence and workflow actions. A later `SATISFACTORY` assessment appends a new version without changing the original adverse assessment or RFI. The Detailed model accepts IA Achievement / IA Not Achieved plus optional comments, findings, recommendation and score. An adverse detailed outcome follows the same mandatory IA-RFI rule. When the configured Audit workflow stage requires a rating, the supplied score is mandatory, must exist in its rating scheme and also appends the normal stage-rating ledger entry.

Versioned `/api/v1/internal-audit` routes expose model history, resolved submission model/history and assessment creation. Configuration uses the dynamic `WORKFLOW.CONFIGURE` policy. Assessment mutation independently checks the OPMS/IPMS `INTERNAL_AUDIT` action through the central scope engine; history reads require the scoped submission READ permission, so hiding an auditor control cannot authorize a direct request. Tenant query filters and write guards cover both new tables. Configuration deletion and assessment mutation/deletion are rejected by DbContext governance.

The Workflow Governance SPA has an Internal Audit tab for tenant/year model selection and complete version history. The auditor queue adds the model-specific form to the selected submission. The simplified form renders only the two specified assessment fields; an adverse choice conditionally requires the IA RFI Due Date. The Detailed form exposes its permitted narratives and score. Both show ordered immutable assessment/RFI history, actor/time evidence and reassessment behavior.

**Migration and tests:** SQL Server migration `20261003145227_V39InternalAuditAssessmentModels` adds both tenant-owned tables, restricted foreign keys, native RowVersion for configuration, date checks, public/business-key indexes, one-current-selection uniqueness and reassessment-chain uniqueness. Six focused relational/controller tests prove model versioning, audit and RowVersion transport, exact simplified-field validation, mandatory adverse due date, atomic RFI creation, configured rating-scheme enforcement, append-only reassessment, direct API denial and immutable history. Eight focused frontend tests across the assessment, queue and governance surfaces pass. The complete backend suite passes **287/287** with one explicitly environment-gated native SQL Server acceptance test skipped; the complete frontend suite passes **142/142 across 43 files**. TypeScript, ESLint, production build, SQL Server model/snapshot consistency and `git diff --check` pass.

**Status:** Both required Internal Audit assessment models, tenant/year selection, model-specific validation, RFI/workflow/rating integration, append-only history and production SPA capture are **COMPLIANT** at repository level. ### 11.69 Configurable reminder, escalation, working-calendar and SMS policies

The remaining repository-controlled notification-policy gap is closed:

### 11.79 Tenant-scoped dynamic user administration and protected contact members

The legacy user-administration boundary now participates in the database-driven security model instead of treating one broad UI permission as authority for every operation:

- User list/detail, create, update, soft-delete, enable/disable, role, scope, assignment and effective-permission calls independently enforce stable `USER`, `ROLE` and `SECURITY` resource/action permissions. Direct API calls are denied when the corresponding capability is absent.
- Every target-user lookup is constrained to the selected municipality. Mutations require an explicit municipality context, new users inherit that municipality, tenant roles cannot be assigned across municipalities, and department/unit scope identifiers are validated through tenant-filtered master queries.
- `USER.Email` and `USER.PhoneNumber` are idempotently registered as sensitive members with independent READ/UPDATE permissions. Responses redact denied values, phone mutation is rejected when its member UPDATE is denied, and the SPA hides the denied email column/contact controls and mutation actions from the same effective capability set.
- User create/update/status, role, scope and assignment changes append contextual audit records. Existing `Admin.Users.Manage` grants are additively migrated to the stable permissions; no administrator-authored role rule is reset.
- Relational SQLite tests prove idempotent registry seeding, member metadata/permissions, tenant-before-projection list behavior, cross-tenant detail denial and direct phone-update denial. A component test proves denied contact data and mutation controls are not rendered.

The complete suites pass **318 backend tests**, with one environment-gated SQL Server test skipped, and **156/156 frontend tests across 48 files**. This adds a third end-to-end protected member path. R-08 remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** because the catalogue is not yet exhaustive across every secondary resource and deployment-level HTTP privilege-escalation testing remains outstanding.

### 11.80 Retirement of parallel legacy role and permission mutation

The remaining legacy security-administration bypass has been removed:

- `GET /api/roles` and its role/permission detail reads now require `SECURITY.VIEW` and constrain non-system callers to the selected municipality. A role identifier from another municipality resolves as not found.
- Legacy role create/update/deactivate and role-permission replacement return HTTP 410 with the versioned `/api/v1/security` replacement contract. They can no longer create ownerless roles, bypass RowVersion, omit audit or modify a role outside the selected municipality.
- Legacy permission-definition POST/PUT/DELETE calls return HTTP 410 and cannot rewrite or remove stable registry codes. Registry definitions remain controlled by the idempotent application registry; administrator-configured role rules continue through the audited, RowVersion-protected security API.
- The old role and permission browser routes now render `SecurityAdministrationPage`, so users receive the governed tenant-role, assignment, ALLOW/DENY/scope, member, action and navigation experience rather than the retired forms. Compatibility grants for the former admin permissions are additively mapped to the stable `SECURITY.*` capabilities without resetting administrator rules.
- Relational tests prove tenant-filtered legacy reads, cross-tenant not-found behavior, HTTP 410 for every legacy mutation and unchanged persisted role/permission data after attempted bypasses.

The complete backend suite passes **320 tests**, with one environment-gated SQL Server test skipped. The existing frontend suite remains **156/156 across 48 files**, and focused routing/security-administration tests pass. R-08 remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** for the still-incomplete member catalogue and deployment-level penetration/privilege-escalation acceptance, but the repository now has one authoritative security-mutation path.

### 11.81 Period-based KPI ordering and governed resequencing

The V3.9 SDBIP sequencing rule is now persisted and enforced rather than inferred from indicator text:

- OPMS and IPMS KPIs carry independent positive `OriginalOrderNumber` and `RevisedOrderNumber` values. New records default revised order to original order, while migration `20261004031802_V39PeriodBasedKpiOrdering` deterministically backfills both values per municipality using creation time and stable public ID before adding constraints and tenant/order indexes.
- Effective-order register queries require an explicit reporting-period type. Q1, Q2 and Mid-Term sort by original order; Q3, Q4 and Annual sort by revised order. Duplicate business order values are permitted and use `PublicId` as the deterministic tie-breaker.
- Performance CSV export rows use the same period-effective rule rather than indicator-number sorting. The rule applies independently of the generic `IsRevised` flag, so an otherwise unchanged KPI can move in the approved revised SDBIP sequence.
- OPMS/IPMS ordering changes use dedicated permission- and scope-protected endpoints with mandatory reason, approval reference, effective date and RowVersion. Each changed order field appends an immutable tenant-owned `KpiFieldRevision`; stale writes fail with conflict and withdrawn KPIs remain immutable.
- The KPI detail UI explains the two period regimes, exposes both values only as editable controls to users with the relevant dynamic UPDATE capability, and displays immutable revision history to authorized readers.
- Six relational tests prove the original/revised switch in reports and paged registers, mandatory period context, OPMS/IPMS field-specific append-only history, stale RowVersion rejection, cross-tenant not-found behavior, positive ordering constraints and unambiguous revision ownership. A component test proves the governed revision payload and history experience.

The complete suites pass **326 backend tests**, with one environment-gated SQL Server test skipped, and **157/157 frontend tests across 49 files**. TypeScript, ESLint, the Release/backend and production/frontend builds, model consistency and idempotent SQL generation pass. Area 10 remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** only because equivalent field-specific governed revision ledgers are not yet complete for every independently revisable KPI metadata field; the period-based ordering requirement itself is repository-complete.

### 11.82 Independent KPI-definition and period-value revisions

The remaining repository-level V3.9 revision gap is closed without reusing the ambiguous generic `IsRevised` switch:

- OPMS and IPMS KPIs persist independent flags and revised values for KPI number, target name and KPI wording while retaining each original. Canonical period rows independently persist revised target/unit and revised applicable budget state.
- A central resolver applies originals to Q1, Q2 and Mid-Term and only independently flagged values to Q3, Q4 and Annual. Registers, selectors, submission pages, workflow queues, consolidation calculations, transient exports and immutable official report generation use the same period-aware rule.
- General KPI edits cannot overwrite original KPI number/name/wording or canonical period values. Dedicated OPMS/IPMS revision endpoints require the dynamic `*.REVISE` action, record external approval metadata, apply tenant/record scope, reject meaningless revised-equals-original values, protect writes with RowVersion and append immutable field history. Ordering and definition histories are returned separately.
- Q1/Q2/Mid-Term target/unit/budget revision flags are rejected server-side. Late-period target and budget flags remain independent, original values are never overwritten, and removing a flag returns the effective value to its original through another auditable revision event.
- The KPI detail UI exposes the independent controls only when the effective revision action is granted, clearly explains the period rule, preserves original/revised display and shows immutable approval history. Hidden controls do not replace server authorization.
- Additive migration `20261004144941_V39FieldSpecificKpiRevisions` introduces only bounded nullable revised values and false-default flags; it does not manufacture revision history or overwrite administrator data.
- Relational tests prove independent OPMS/IPMS field persistence, filtered immutable history, stale-writer rejection and early/late resolution. Component tests prove the independently flagged payload, action-driven UI and history experience.

With full-suite verification recorded below, R-22 and assessment area 10 are **COMPLIANT** at repository level. Native SQL Server application and concurrency evidence remains explicitly isolated under area 31 rather than inferred from SQLite.

The complete suites pass **330 backend tests**, with one environment-gated SQL Server test skipped, and **158/158 frontend tests across 50 files**. TypeScript, ESLint, the Release/backend and production/frontend builds, bundle budget, model consistency and idempotent SQL generation pass.

### 11.83 End-to-end HTTP tenant-isolation matrix

The missing single-scenario repository proof now runs through the real ASP.NET Core test host rather than invoking controllers directly:

- A disposable relational SQLite database creates two municipalities, their departments, users, targets, submissions, canonical period targets, POE metadata and audit rows. The Municipality A operator, tenant role and permissions are created dynamically in the database.
- The authenticated request traverses CSRF, authentication, tenant resolution, dynamic permission evaluation, global EF query filters, controllers, formatters and idempotency. The test proves Municipality A's target register excludes Municipality B, direct target fetch returns not found, and direct submission edit and approval attempts cannot resolve the Municipality B record.
- Multipart POE upload and protected content-download attempts against Municipality B return not found before storage access. The performance summary contains exactly Municipality A's target, submission and department, and the paged audit response contains Municipality A evidence without Municipality B evidence.
- A second HTTP test supplies Municipality B through `X-Municipality-Id`; tenant resolution rejects the forged selection with 403 `TENANT_CONTEXT_DENIED` before controller execution.
- `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` hosts the actual application entry point. Test-only authentication changes no production authentication path, the database and evidence directory are unique per test and removed after connection-pool release, and all application queries remain provider-neutral for SQL Server deployment.

The focused HTTP suite passes **2/2** and the complete backend suite passes **332 tests**, with one environment-gated native SQL Server test skipped. R-02 and final assessment area 2 are now **COMPLIANT** at repository level. Native SQL Server execution remains separately classified as Not Verifiable under area 31, and deployed penetration/UAT evidence remains under areas 4 and 32.

Each class has an allow-listed column contract and class-specific headings; a template lineage cannot change class.

### 11.85 Durable asynchronous report generation, scheduling and distribution

The remaining repository-controlled R-41 scheduling and distribution gap is closed:

- `OfficialReportJob` is a durable municipality-owned queue record with exact template/FY/period/filter inputs, retry and processing state, attempt/timing/error evidence, requester identity, recipient/channel snapshot, immutable result-generation link and SQL Server `rowversion`. Stale processing work is recovered and transient failures use bounded retry; authorization or validation failures terminate without generating output.
- `OfficialReportSchedule` is an immutable version lineage with Once/Daily/Weekly/Monthly cadence, interval, next occurrence, effective bounds, active state, approval reference, reason, department/unit filters, dynamic user/role recipients and IN_APP/EMAIL/SMS channels. Editing appends a successor instead of rewriting history, and schedule occurrence uniqueness prevents duplicate materialization after downtime or concurrent polling.
- The hosted worker calls the same secured official-generation action used by direct requests, under the persisted requester and municipality context. Report GENERATE, KPI READ, submission READ, record scope and Audit Trail permission are therefore re-evaluated at execution; a hidden UI action cannot bypass the API, and cross-municipality data cannot be selected.
- Successful jobs link the new immutable `OfficialReportGeneration`, create `ReportReady` in-app notifications, and enqueue the existing governed delivery outbox with recipient/channel snapshots. The outbox link supplies retry and receipt evidence; schedules with no effective recipients fail closed.
- `/api/v1/reports/official/jobs` and `/schedules` expose bounded job history, queue, retry, versioned schedule save and run-now operations with dynamic permission checks, exact tenant-owned foreign-key validation, reasons, audit and RowVersion conflict handling. The Reports SPA exposes immediate queueing, generation-version queueing, job state/error/delivery history, schedule versioning and failed-job retry without treating button visibility as authorization.
- Migration `20261004170828_V39OfficialReportJobsAndDistribution` adds only the two governed tables, restricted tenant/template/year/period/filter/generation/outbox relationships, cadence/state/check constraints, version/occurrence uniqueness and native SQL Server rowversions. Four relational tests prove successful scheduled generation and distribution, zero-recipient fail-closed behavior, direct queue denial without underlying resource permission, and RowVersion-protected schedule succession.

**Status:** R-41 is **COMPLIANT at repository level**. Production provider delivery, representative-volume performance and native SQL Server execution remain deployment acceptance evidence rather than missing repository functionality.

### 11.86 Municipality/year-configurable SDBIP layers

The previously missing SDBIP-layer foundation is now implemented without introducing a provider-specific application path:

- `SdbipLayer` is a tenant-owned, financial-year-specific controlled master with stable public identity, normalized code, administrator-defined display name and order, soft-active state, audit timestamps and RowVersion. Composite foreign keys prevent a layer from referencing another municipality's year and prevent an OPMS KPI from referencing another municipality's layer.
- Versioned master endpoints and the Tenant Calendar administration surface support create, read and reasoned update/deactivation under dynamic `SDBIP_LAYER` CRUD permissions. Duplicate codes are rejected per municipality financial year, stale updates conflict, and a layer with active non-withdrawn KPIs cannot be deactivated.
- OPMS create and update resolve the selected layer by public ID, require it to be active and to belong to the exact municipality financial year selected through the canonical period plan, and return layer identity in the public response. The target form loads active persisted layers and filters them by the selected fiscal year; direct API calls retain the same enforcement.
- Migration `20261004175415_V39GovernedSdbipLayers` creates the governed master, composite alternate/foreign keys, uniqueness and ordering indexes, native SQL Server RowVersion, and a nullable legacy-cutover `OpmsTargets.SdbipLayerId`. New writes require the relationship; historic rows remain nullable until controlled reconciliation so the migration does not invent layer ownership.

Two focused relational tests prove audited administration, tenant filtering, duplicate prevention, composite cross-tenant rejection, portable stale-writer behavior and protected deactivation. Existing normalized-target tests now prove persistence through the required layer relationship, while the administration test proves production API transport. The complete suites pass **341 backend tests** with one explicitly environment-gated SQL Server test skipped and **158/158 frontend tests across 50 files**.

This closes the repository-controlled configurable-layer and exact-year target-association prerequisite. Area 18 remains **PARTIALLY COMPLIANT** because bulk OPMS/SDBIP import, row-level validation/reconciliation and historic target-to-layer assignment are separate open work.

## SQL Server Revalidation Required

SQLite remains an interim development and relational-test provider. Before production readiness is claimed, execute and retain evidence for the following against a positively identified SQL Server/Azure SQL environment:

- clean and upgrade application of every committed migration, including `20261002204550_V39CanonicalSubmissionBaseState`, its legacy-state backfill, `20261003145227_V39InternalAuditAssessmentModels`, `20261003152131_V39OfficialReportGeneration`, `20261003160701_V39NotificationPoliciesAndScheduling`, `20261003161402_V39NotificationPreferences`, `20261003170339_V39CanonicalActualPerformanceCutover`, `20261003230747_V39TenantScopedPagedAudit`, `20261004031802_V39PeriodBasedKpiOrdering`, `20261004144941_V39FieldSpecificKpiRevisions`, `20261004161339_V39OfficialReportFamilies`, `20261004170828_V39OfficialReportJobsAndDistribution` and `20261004175415_V39GovernedSdbipLayers`;
- native generated `rowversion`, stale-writer conflicts and all filtered/unique/check indexes;
- decimal precision, UTC/date behavior, restricted cascades and workflow/audit transaction rollback;
- tenant/security query plans, bounded register load behavior, locking and concurrency under representative volume;
- security persistence, permission revocation, direct HTTP bypass attempts and delegated-administrator privilege-escalation tests;
- backup, checksum, isolated restore, integrity verification, measured RPO/RTO and failover rehearsal.

Successful SQLite tests do not certify these SQL Server behaviors. Provider cutover remains configuration plus migrations; no SQLite-specific domain model or authorization path was introduced.

### 11.229 Target-library creation, session-concurrency and edit-reference repair

Session validation now reloads after a stale activity touch, permits the request only when the winning session remains active, unexpired and security-stamp-valid, and continues to fail closed when the competing operation is sign-out or revocation. Third, the edit form bound name-backed template references to empty identifiers, causing persisted units and strategic/budget selections to display the wrong defaults and risk destructive overwrite. OPMS and IPMS edit initialization now resolve persisted names to the current governed lookup identifiers case-insensitively.

Final browser warning/error output was empty.

### 11.244 Period-target member security and direct-write enforcement

The live OPMS/IPMS reporting-period target, budget and description fields are now independently registered as sensitive members on both KPI resources. ### 11.305 Deterministic official-report worker recovery and dispatch ordering

Starting the persisted local SQLite verification application exposed EF Core's `RowLimitingOperationWithoutOrderByWarning` in the official-report background worker. Interrupted `Processing` jobs were limited to 25 rows without an order, so the recovery set depended on provider execution order. Due schedules and ready jobs had primary time ordering but no unique tie-breaker, allowing equal timestamps to produce unstable batch membership between executions.

Interrupted leases now recover oldest `StartedAt` first and use the internal primary key only as a deterministic tie-breaker. Ready jobs retain `AvailableAt`/`RequestedAt` priority and add the same stable tie-breaker; due schedules likewise use `NextRunAt` followed by the primary key. These ordering keys remain internal query mechanics and do not alter public contracts, authorization, schedule semantics or provider behavior.

The relational due-schedule/worker test now promotes EF's unordered row-limiting diagnostic to an exception, so any worker query that reintroduces `Take` without ordering fails the suite. The end-to-end worker scenario passes **1/1**, the complete official-report job suite passes **12/12**, and complete regression passes **678 backend tests with 1 explicit SQL Server-only skip and 0 failures**. Release compilation completes with **0 warnings and 0 errors**, and diff hygiene passes. The running SQLite application returned HTTP 200 from its liveness endpoint before browser inspection was attempted. No schema migration, frontend change or provider-specific application branch is introduced.

### 11.312 Atomic POE association, scan and disposal history

POE assessment, replacement, legal-hold and disposal child records were already append-only, but the parent association and shared physical-blob metadata remained directly mutable. A data-context caller could hard-delete either parent, rewrite file/submission/storage/signature provenance, retire or reactivate an association without replacement evidence, attach predecessor lineage without its ledger, or mark physical content deleted without a completed disposal event. POE controller mutations also saved the business change before a separate audit save, leaving a process-failure window in which successful evidence governance could exist without its corresponding audit.

The persistence boundary now rejects `PoeFile` and `EvidenceBlob` hard deletion and freezes their tenant, submission, upload, storage, content, signature and creation identity. Every appended assessment, replacement, legal-hold and disposal row must resolve to a parent file owned by the same municipality. An active POE association may retire only beside exactly one same-municipality, same-submission append-only replacement record in the same unit of work; its successor may acquire predecessor lineage exactly once beside that same ledger, and retired evidence cannot be reactivated. Physical scan state may change only for available content with a non-empty result and monotonic scan timestamp. Content deletion is one-way, timestamped and requires exactly one matching completed disposal event in the same transaction. OPMS/IPMS upload, rescan, assessment, replacement, legal-hold placement/release and disposal request paths now queue their reasoned audit evidence before the mutation save; upload notifications/outbox evidence are queued in that transaction as well.

### 11.318 Readable and native-compatible official report documents

The official PDF renderer previously flattened every record into a single pipe-delimited line, discarded content after 160 characters and used fixed row counts rather than measured content. The DOCX and XLSX packages were structurally minimal and supplied no governed visual hierarchy, intentional widths, wrapping, repeating headers or print behavior. All three official document formats now render the same canonical dataset as readable landscape tables. PDF uses weighted columns, measured word wrapping, variable-height pagination, repeated title/header context, alternating row shading, borders and page numbers without arbitrary value truncation; common Unicode punctuation and diacritics are normalized safely for its embedded WinAnsi base fonts. DOCX uses a fixed landscape grid, explicit widths and margins, repeating blue table headers, non-splitting rows, cell padding, wrapping and alternating shading. XLSX supplies a complete workbook view and style table, a merged report title, frozen first two rows, explicit widths, wrapped/bordered banded rows, filtering, landscape fit-to-width settings and print-title rows. Its XML now follows the schema-defined child order, and regression coverage fixes that ordering as a contract.

A representative 70-row municipality report was rendered in every format. The three-page PDF was rasterized and every page visually inspected, including repeated headings, complete wrapped values and page numbering. The generated DOCX opened in desktop Microsoft Word without repair, exported as four landscape pages and visually retained its header on every page. The generated XLSX opened in desktop Microsoft Excel without repair, retained frozen/filtered styled content and exported as three landscape pages with repeated print headers. ### 11.435 Optional-verifier bypass and governed correction/resubmission

The configurable workflow now implements the V3.9 optional-verifier rule as an explicit permission-controlled approver command. `APPROVE_BYPASS` is accepted only when the current stage is both optional and configured to allow bypass, the immediately following active stage is an approval stage, and the approval-stage segregation and rating rules succeed. One append-only action records the verifier-stage origin, bypass outcome, authenticated approver, reason/rating, correlation identity and resulting post-approval stage; it does not manufacture a verifier action or overwrite history. OPMS and IPMS expose separate versioned commands and dynamic security actions, and the client displays the bypass control only from the server-projected stage configuration.

Submitted correction is now a two-command governed lifecycle rather than a mutable status shortcut. `CORRECT` requires its own action permission and a protected non-empty workflow comment, appends a `Reopen` action at the current configured stage, and returns only the base-state projection to `IN_PROGRESS`. Authorized scoped editors can then update the permitted Actual Performance, Variance Reason and Corrective Measure members through the ordinary audited edit boundary. `RESUBMIT` is valid only from workflow `Rework`, re-runs submission completeness, POE and reporting-window validation, appends a distinct `Resubmit` action, returns the base state to `SUBMITTED`, and either leaves the item at its configured review stage or advances from an explicit Submit rework stage. Previous submissions, rejections, corrections and actor evidence remain append-preserved.

The former hard-coded owner predicate no longer overrides dynamic record/member security for an in-progress submission. The API still requires the resource UPDATE permission, record/tenant/assignment scope, exact member UPDATE decisions and base-state guard, allowing effective reassignment, additional submitters and appropriately authorized approvers without broadening cross-tenant access. New security actions and legacy-role mappings are additive and idempotent; administrator, approver and submitter defaults receive only their intended correction, resubmission or bypass capabilities.

### 11.471 Durable operational-alert transitions and delivery handoff

The System Operations workspace previously exposed only a point-in-time readiness snapshot. Configured recipient PublicIds are resolved to active internal users at persistence time and are never exposed by the API. Channels are restricted to the existing `IN_APP`, `EMAIL` and `SMS` delivery contracts. If no recipients are configured, the transition is still append-preserved and cleanly processed as history-only evidence, preserving an integration point for later SIEM/export collection. The existing notification worker supplies idempotent delivery attempts and receipts. The permission-gated overview now returns at most 20 recent transitions, bounded internally to 50, with only public event/incident identities, lifecycle/status/check names, occurrence time and aggregate delivered/failed/terminal counts. A database/history failure degrades only the history panel and does not hide live readiness. The API discloses only whether recipients are configured, not their identities or destinations. Monitoring is disabled in base/local configuration to prevent fabricated development alerts and enabled explicitly by production configuration; the poll interval, recipient PublicIds and channels remain environment configuration.

GitHub CLI and hosted-workflow status are no longer required to decide whether a development cycle is complete. `tools/Invoke-LocalQualityGate.ps1` now provides a fail-fast repository-owned verifier for the same substantive gates: backend/test restore, Release build, the complete backend suite, non-empty idempotent EF migration scripting, SQL Server and SQLite recovery safety contracts, representative performance-acceptance safety validation, backend vulnerability audit, clean frontend dependency installation, TypeScript, ESLint, the complete frontend suite, accessibility, production build/bundle budget, frontend vulnerability audit and a tracked-file credential-shape scan that reports only filenames and never matching content. `-SkipRestore` omits only dependency restoration/installation when lock files are unchanged; it does not omit any build, test, migration, audit, safety, accessibility or bundle check. This checkout has the hook installed. A nested-invocation guard prevents accidental recursion. ### 11.476 Three-municipality configuration acceptance matrix

V3.9 sections 41–42 require acceptance against at least three differently configured municipalities rather than treating a single default seed as proof of configurability. `ThreeMunicipalityAcceptanceMatrixTests` now creates three profiles concurrently in one relational SQLite database: a local-authentication municipality with TID disabled and a one-stage no-rating workflow; a Microsoft Entra ID municipality with optional TID and ratings at every workflow stage; and a hybrid-authentication municipality with mandatory all-KPI TID, an optional verifier stage, approver bypass and a deliberately non-ordinal binary rating scheme. The test uses only persisted configuration and the production workflow service—no profile-specific application branches or recompilation.

Each profile executes and persists its configured workflow. The local profile completes with one unrated submit action; the enterprise profile retains two independently rated actions; and the hybrid profile projects the configured bypass capability, records one auditable bypass action and resolves binary value `0` to its configured `Target met` snapshot even though value `1` is labelled `Target not met`. ### 11.513 Financial-year-scoped persistent workflow queue filters

V3.9 section 35.5 requires Verification, Approval, PMS, Internal Audit, RFI and personal workflow queues to use server-side filters and search, retaining the user's filter state for the browser session where appropriate. The combined workflow queue previously applied dynamic record scope and database paging, but accepted only a queue name and page. Users could not search or narrow the result set by financial year, framework, period or canonical workflow state, and no queue filter survived navigation during the session.

The versioned workflow-queue request now validates a bounded 200-character search term, municipality financial-year PublicId, OPMS/IPMS framework, period, canonical state, six allowlisted sort fields and ascending/descending direction. Filtering occurs after tenant/dynamic-scope intersection and queue selection but before SQL count, ordering and paging. Search deliberately covers only KPI name and indicator number, so protected submitter, verifier and approver identities cannot be inferred through result counts. Ordering always adds framework and internal record identity as stable tie-breakers. Read-only normalization helpers are no longer published as false client query parameters in the generated OpenAPI contract.

Both governed and personal workflow queue screens now expose the same accessible server-backed filter surface. Municipality financial years use the bounded active-year picker; framework, period, state and sort controls use allowlisted values; Reset restores the exact default server query. Each queue stores its own validated filter state in `sessionStorage`, restores it when the user returns during the same browser session and resets paging whenever a filter changes. Invalid or unavailable stored values fail closed to defaults rather than being sent to the API. OPMS and IPMS dashboard verification/approval cards now deep-link the exact selected financial year and framework; those explicit link parameters override an older session filter and become the restored queue context.

### 11.514 Assignment-aware actionable RFI queue

V3.9 section 35.5 requires a distinct RFI queue alongside Verification, Approval, PMS and Internal Audit, with records limited to the user's responsibility/scope, action readiness represented separately, no bulk workflow decisions, and server-side session-persistent filters where appropriate. The application previously exposed governed RFI histories only inside one selected submission plus a read-oriented Outstanding RFI report. It did not provide a cross-submission operational queue from which an authorised responder or closer could identify and open the exact RFI requiring action.

Hidden UI therefore does not replace direct API enforcement.

### 11.515 Persistent application financial-year context

**SOFTWARE IMPLEMENTATION: SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLIANT — EXTERNAL ACCEPTANCE REMAINS.**

**PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE: NOT PRODUCTION READY.**

The repository contains substantial, tested implementation for tenant-aware security, configurable workflows, governed submissions, POE handling, global National KPA/Back-to-Basics references, municipality/year-scoped strategic planning masters, canonical seven-reference OPMS/IPMS KPI classification, governed KPI/indicator/functional/standard/unit classifications, optional hierarchy relationships, governed budget types and multi-source budget allocations, effective-dated strategic risks, accountable owners, immutable risk assessments/reviews, governed treatments, heatmap/report projections and KPI relationships, TID, Circular 88, IDP, audit, notification operations and bounded registers. All executable repository quality gates available in this environment pass. Those facts do not close the remaining V3.9 product gaps or the deployment evidence gaps. Fixture-backed generic lookup routes have been retired or mapped to authoritative administration, and new OPMS/IPMS target writes use normalized period records plus governed strategic, performance-classification, display-unit and budget foreign keys with controlled historic reconciliation. Mid-Term/Annual suggestions now have central calculation, separate suggested/final persistence, immutable history, protected APIs and a production SPA workflow. Both configurable Internal Audit models now have governed tenant/year selection, model-specific capture, RFI/rating integration and immutable reassessment history. Official reports now cover all 16 required classes through versioned approved templates, immutable stored CSV/XLSX/DOCX/PDF output, durable asynchronous jobs, versioned schedules, dynamic recipients, delivery evidence, snapshot hashes and execution/download re-authorization. Notification policies now provide versioned inheritance, working-calendar reminders/escalations, downtime catch-up, SMS, persisted preferences and terminal missing-address handling. Live local SQLite evidence plus exact `localhost\SQLEXPRESS` migration, trusted-constraint, dynamic-security, native-concurrency, historical-cutover, 20,000-row load and checksum recovery acceptance now supply measured repository evidence. Production-shaped upgrade/cutover, production operational integrations and external assurance remain unexecuted.
